newsitem.title: UK: "Watch and wait," urges C&W after DT comments.
newsitem.headline: "Watch and wait," urges C&W after DT comments.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Plc urged investors to "watch and wait" on Wednesday after Deutsche Telekom AG said the two firms were in talks -- but also cautioned that this did not point to any imminent deal.

C&W, Britain's second biggest telecoms group, has said it is in talks with "everybody" including Global One, the marriage of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and America's Sprint -- and AT&T, with its Unisource/World Partners global alliance.
"We're talking to people all the time," a spokeswoman told Reuters. "(People will) just have to watch and wait."
Late on Tuesday, Deutsche Telekom chairman Ron Sommer told reporters that "everyone is flirting with everyone" and no conclusions could be drawn from the fact that talks were being held with C&W.

Some analysts tip C&W, with its British operations and what some call the most attractive asset base available in Asia, as being the most sought-after partner for telecoms alliances that are trying to plug geographic gaps in their portfolios.

Global One, which has said that it wants to have the broadest geographical coverage, lacks assets in both Britain and in the booming Asia Pacific region. Equally, analysts say local U.S. telephone operators, or regional bells (RBOCs), may also be keen to link up with international companies such as C&W.
"I wouldn't rule out an alliance with an RBOC merger and/or Global One over the coming months," said Simon Carrington, telecoms analyst at Merrill Lynch.
"But I don't think the Global One deal is imminent -- for example within four weeks. We do feel, however, that something will be sealed by the winter."

Brokers Salomon Brothers likes comparing companies such as C&W to the prettiest girl at a dance for partners which has been triggered by the imminent liberalisation of most of the world telecoms markets.

"To AT&T Unisource, to (America's) MFS WorldCom, to Bell Atlantic /NYNEX, to any of the people needing to establish a global asset base, C&W has got to be the most attractive asset base available," the broker says.
Salomon Brothers telecoms analyst Andrew Harrington believes that for this reason, the likely source of the next big deal in telecoms will be "some sort of equity stake" taken in C&W.
C&W withdrew from its German telecoms alliance with Veba AG and RWE AG earlier this month to focus on its new British-based cable venture, Cable and Wireless Communications.

The retreat from Germany followed last year's decision, under new chief executive Dick Brown, to abandon an alliance with Italian telecoms holding company STET and forego bidding on the key fixed-line contract with French railway company SNCF.
These moves have freed up capital that analysts say the company can pour into its British and Hong Kong operations.
But they say it also opens the door to cooperation with an international alliance like Global One.
Deutsche Telekom chairman Summers has been quoted as saying he is "excited to see Dick Brown taking major steps to become a serious contender to British Telecommunications ."

C&W plans to tackle BT, the dominant British player, via its new Cable and Wireless Communications venture -- a merger of its British Mercury business with cable television operators Nynex CableComms Group Plc, Bell Cablemedia Plc and Videotron Holdings.
